text:
Probably yes, if closing costs are under about $9-10k.

On a fresh 30-year term, the payment drops from about $2,529 to $2,373, saving roughly $156/month. Typical closing costs of 2-3% ($8-12k) put breakeven around 4.5-6.5 years. Over your 10 years you'd net roughly $7-10k, more if costs are low. A rate cut of 0.6 points is a bit under the old 0.75-1 point rule of thumb, so the costs decide it.

The strongest case against is term reset. If you're several years into your current loan, a new 30-year term can raise lifetime interest even at a lower rate. Choose a term matching your remaining years (or keep paying your old payment amount) so the savings go to principal rather than being absorbed by a longer schedule. The other risk is rates falling further, but you can refinance again, and a no-cost or low-cost option (lender credit at a slightly higher rate) limits the downside.

It flips to no if costs exceed about $12k, if you might move before roughly year 5, or if your current loan is near payoff.

I assumed your existing payment is the standard 30-year amount; send your actual remaining term and quoted closing costs for an exact breakeven.
